assertions.evidence: All four test methods include @TableTest(""" ... """) annotations

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 combines fulfillment type and address into one method: '@DisplayName("Group items by fulfillment type and delivery address")' tests both concerns together, not separately

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 7 rows mixing fulfillment and address. Rows like 'Same address stays together' test address logic only with DELIVERY type, creating unnecessary permutations from combining separate concerns

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items with different fulfillment types (store pickup vs home delivery) cannot share a shipment.
assertions.evidence: Fulfillment method is tested in Table 1 combined with address: 'shouldGroupItemsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress'. Expected output specifies five separate concerns; model has four

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items going to different addresses must be in separate shipments.
assertions.evidence: Address splitting is tested in Table 1 combined with fulfillment type: 'shouldGroupItemsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress'. Expected output requires 'five concerns' as separate tables

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — in-stock items ship immediately, backordered/pre-ordered items ship when available.
assertions.evidence: Method 'shouldSplitByAvailability' with 6 rows dedicated to testing availability: 'All in stock ships immediately', 'In-stock not held for backordered', etc.

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation (minimising shipments) is represented as its own @TableTest — choosing which warehouses to ship from to minimise total shipment count.
assertions.evidence: Method 'shouldMinimiseShipmentCount' with 4 rows: 'Single warehouse covers all', 'No single warehouse covers both', 'Two warehouses sufficient, not three'

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest — paired items (e.g. camera body and lens) should ship together from the same location when possible.
assertions.evidence: Method 'shouldKeepCompanionsTogether' with 3 rows: 'Full group at one warehouse', 'Full group at WH1 preferred over split'

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods. All outputs of the same concern belong together.
assertions.evidence: Table 3 includes both 'Shipment count?' and 'Warehouses used?' in same table; Table 2 includes 'Immediate items?' and 'Deferred items?' together

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation table uses scalar quantity columns (e.g. 'Qty ordered') not item lists, when product identity doesn't matter for the logic.
assertions.evidence: Table 3 Items column uses '[P1:1:DELIVERY:Main-St, P2:1:DELIVERY:Main-St]' format; expected output states 'Warehouse allocation uses scalar quantity'

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All four tables have 'Scenario' as leftmost column: 'Single delivery item', 'All in stock ships immediately', etc.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Shipments?', 'Groups?')
assertions.evidence: Multiple output columns: 'Shipment groups?', 'Immediate items?', 'Deferred items?', 'Shipment count?', 'Warehouses used?', 'Companion shipment?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Consolidate: two beats three', 'Everything at one warehouse') — not 'Test case 2'.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names: 'Single delivery item', 'All in stock ships immediately', 'Single warehouse covers all', 'Full group at WH1 preferred over split'

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language (e.g. 'Shipments?' not 'Result?', 'Warehouse stock' not 'inventory_map'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All four test method bodies: shouldGroupItemsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress, shouldSplitByAvailability, shouldMinimiseShipmentCount, shouldKeepCompanionsTogether contain no if/switch

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName annotations: 'Group items by fulfillment type and delivery address', 'Split in-stock items from backordered and pre-ordered items'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description annotations use triple-quoted text blocks: @Description(\"\"\" ... \"\"\")
